title: Bill Beason's beat versus Jo Jones
summary: Clifton Glover found a substitute drummer could not match Jo Jones's feel, which is why Jo played the shows.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yes, it is. Cliff always talks today about how you guys come out of the West and guys come out with that Western lope , that's what he calls it. And there was a drummer here named Beason ? Have you heard of Bill Beason ?

Bill Beason was the drummer that was supposed to play when Cliff was directing the band. Bill Beason was (appointed) to Jo Jones place. And Cliff tells me, he says, man, he says, I give the down beat and Beason's beat does not fit Jo Jones.
So the next show, they just told Beason that Jo said he'd play the rest of the shows.
: Why did they have Beason in the first place?
Well, as I said, at that time there was a law that said ......
: Oh, I see what you mean.
They were supposed to be playing for the shows.
: Yes, he was the New York band.

Yes, yes. And Cliff was directing and Beason. I don't remember who else, who the other guys were in the band. But Cliff talks about it now. How disappointed he was with Beason because he didn't take the band like Jo did.
Especially the difference in the style.
